task: I'm the secretary for the Maple Street Community Garden and we have 6 unused plots that got reassigned from people who never showed up this season. Write a notice to post at the gate explaining that plots left empty past Nov 15 will go to the waitlist of 9 people.
rewrite:
ambition:     Define the cutoff plainly, since "empty" is where gate notices turn into arguments. The notice should give the exact date (Sunday, Nov 15) and one clear way for a current holder to keep a plot. It should also say how many plots and people are involved (6 plots, 9 waiting) so it reads as fair, not arbitrary.
agency:       The raw material is the garden's own plot assignment sheet and waitlist roster. Neither is in reach, so I'll use the facts given (6 plots, 9 waitlisted, Nov 15 cutoff) and leave blanks for plot numbers and the secretary's contact details.
acceleration: Use the inverted-pyramid format for a posted notice: a large headline with the date, one sentence on what happens, one sentence on what to do, then a contact line. Print it at 14pt or larger and post it in a sheet protector so it survives weather.
accuracy:     Show it to one member who hasn't seen it and give them 10 seconds at arm's length. They should be able to say what happens, by when, and who to contact. Check the date against a calendar: Nov 15, 2026 is a Sunday.

deeper task:
Write a one-page notice for the Maple Street Community Garden gate, from the garden secretary, in a friendly neighborly tone that doesn't scold. Open with a large headline that carries the date. Explain that 6 plots that were reassigned from members who never showed up this season are still unused, and that any of these plots still empty after Sunday, Nov 15 will go to the waitlist of 9 people. Tell anyone who still wants their plot to contact the secretary before that date. Put the plot numbers and the secretary's contact details in as blanks to fill in, and invent nothing else. Keep it short enough to read at a glance from the gate.

answers.plain:
**MAPLE STREET COMMUNITY GARDEN**
**NOTICE: Unused Plots**

**Posted:** [date]

Six garden plots were not claimed or planted this season. They have been released by their previous assignees and are now unassigned.

**Deadline: November 15**

Any plot that is still empty after November 15 will be offered to the garden's waitlist. There are currently 9 people waiting.

**If you are a plot holder:**
If you have a plot you plan to use, please plant, tend, or clear it before November 15. If you can't keep your plot, let us know so it can go to someone who will use it.

**Questions or concerns?**
If you think a plot was marked unused by mistake, or you need more time, contact the garden secretary before November 15:

[Name] | [Phone/Email]

Thank you for helping us make the most of every plot.

*Maple Street Community Garden*

---

I left placeholders for the posting date and your contact info. Two things to check before you post it:

- **Plot numbers:** If you list the six affected plots, people can see right away whether theirs is one of them.
- **Exceptions:** I assumed the six plots were released outright. If any previous holders can still reclaim theirs, add a line saying so.

I can also make a shorter, larger-print version for the gate if you'd like.

# Gate notice

**MAPLE STREET COMMUNITY GARDEN**

## 6 Plots Available: Use Them by November 15 or They Go to the Waitlist

**Plots [numbers, e.g. 4, 7, 11, 12, 18, 23]** have gone unused this season. They are open to the people who were assigned to them, and to no one else, until **Sunday, November 15**.

**What this means for you**
- If one of these plots is yours, let us know you want it and start using it before **November 15**.
- Any of the 6 plots that is still empty after November 15 will be reassigned to the **waitlist, which currently has 9 people**. Waitlisted gardeners will be offered plots in the order they signed up.

**What counts as "in use"**
Fall is a good time to plant, so the bar is low. A plot is in use if it has any of these:
- Garlic, overwintering greens, or other fall crops planted
- A cover crop (clover, rye) sown
- Beds cleared of weeds and mulched or covered for winter

**How to keep your plot**
Contact [Name], Secretary, by **[date, e.g. Nov 8]**:
📧 [email]  📞 [phone/text]

Or write your name and plot number on the sign-up sheet in the box at the gate.

If you can't garden this season, please tell us. We will gladly pass the plot to a neighbor who is waiting, and you can rejoin the waitlist for spring.

*Thank you for helping every plot in this garden get used.*
Posted October 26, 2026

---

# Notes on what I assumed

1. **Fill in the brackets.** These are the plot numbers, your contact details, and the "tell us by" date. I suggested a date a week before the deadline so you have time to act before the 15th.
2. **The "in use" definition is my addition.** Without one, "empty" can turn into an argument on November 16. If your bylaws define it, use their wording instead. If you'd rather keep it strict, delete that section.
3. **Who it applies to.** I wrote it for the 6 plots, addressed to their assigned holders. If you meant it as a rule for all plots, change the headline to "Plots left empty past November 15 will go to the waitlist" and drop the plot numbers.
4. **November 15, 2026 is a Sunday.** If you want a weekday deadline, Friday the 13th is the nearest one, but it may put people off. Saturday the 14th is another option.
5. **Waitlist fairness.** Telling people the offers go in sign-up order, and that the list has 9 people, shows the process is transparent. Make sure that's true before you post it.

**Before posting**
- Email or text the assigned holders directly as well. A gate sign alone won't reach people who haven't visited, and that gap is what will draw complaints later.
- Laminate the notice or put it in a sheet protector, and add a few photos of what a "fall-ready" plot looks like if you can.

I can also write a short email or text version for the assigned holders, or the offer message to send the waitlist. Let me know if you want either.
